sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **The Deadline**: Attlee announced that the British would leave India by **June 1948**, regardless of whether a consensus was reached between the INC and the Muslim League.
• **The Shift**: The declaration signaled a shift from 'negotiated settlement' to 'expedited withdrawal' to avoid a civil war scenario.
• **The Appointment**: Lord Mountbatten was appointed as the last Viceroy to oversee the transfer of power, replacing Lord Wavell.
• **Key Metric**: The British government recognized that the **administrative machinery** (ICS/Police) was exhausted and the **financial burden** of maintaining the Indian Empire was unsustainable post-WWII.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Fixed June 1948 deadline; promised transfer to 'responsible Indian hands'.
Labour Party's anti-imperialist stance & economic exhaustion.
Prelims: Date and intent of the declaration.
Partition of India; Dominion status; Princely states given choice.
Failure of interim government to function; communal riots.
Mains: Impact on integration of Princely States.

items.definition: The constitutional status where India would remain part of the British Commonwealth with the British Monarch as the symbolic head, a key compromise to ensure a smooth transition.
The British doctrine governing relations with Princely States; Attlee declared that paramountcy would lapse upon transfer of power, leaving states legally independent.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Indian Independence Act 1947**: The legislative embodiment of the transfer of power, passed by the British Parliament in July 1947.
• **Boundary Commission**: Radcliffe Commission established to demarcate the borders of Punjab and Bengal.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Communal violence, administrative breakdown, and the integration of 565+ Princely States.
• **Solutions**: The 'Standstill Agreement' and the diplomatic efforts of Sardar Patel to ensure accession.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'F-A-M-E' (Feb-Attlee-Mountbatten-Exit).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Feb 1947 (Attlee's Declaration) -> Mountbatten arrives -> Exit of British (Aug 1947).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'June 1948' deadline (Attlee's declaration) with the actual date of independence (August 1947). The declaration did not mandate partition, but the subsequent political deadlock made it inevitable.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Strategic Retreat' to describe the British withdrawal. It was not a defeat, but a calculated exit to preserve British economic interests in the Commonwealth.

keyTakeaways: Attlee's declaration was a pragmatic response to the post-war decline of British imperial power.
The declaration effectively ended the 'Cabinet Mission' approach of keeping India united.
The lapse of paramountcy created a constitutional vacuum that necessitated the rapid integration of Princely States.
